added_failures_note: unmeasured: the reviewed run's manifest declares baseline_suite null and after_suite null -- its evidence was a data benchmark emitting a JSON receipt, not a pytest suite -- so no gate log exists from which to take an added-failure count; the schema records this as unmeasured, never as zero.

findings.text: the m-family loops 10-12 are reported unreachable through a zero-padding mismatch, not through an absence on the machine: loop_identities() builds the raw channel as f"sad_out_{family}{number:02d}" (tag line 71, raw_channel line 77), giving sad_out_m10/m11/m12, while the level-1 store spells those three loops three-digit as sad_out_m010/m011/m012. Verified over the receipt's own 86-shot cohort: sad_out_m010, sad_out_m011 and sad_out_m012 are present at the same 26 shots (range 15051-25836) as sad_out_m09, and sad_out_m10/m11/m12 at none; the l and u families are two-digit and unaffected. The receipt records raw_shot_count 0 for saddle_m_10..m_12 against 26 for m_1..m_9, so the node's headline "33 of 36 reconciled, m_10..m_12 unreachable" and its follow-on "confirm whether m_10..m_12 exist under a distinct channel name" are both wrong; the true count is 36/36. Repair by resolving each loop's raw key from the store's own key set, or by probing the m-family three-digit spelling, rather than assuming one fixed width across families.

the paragraph contradicts the receipt it cites: it states that every l and u loop and m_1-m_9 are present at the same 26 cohort shots, but docs/figures/mast-saddle-loops/reach.json records 3-shot reachability (range 25818-25836) for l_3..l_12 (10 loops) and u_2..u_6,u_8..u_12 (10 loops), with only l_1, l_2, u_1 and u_7 at 26; the same sentence then names l_3/l_4 at 3 shots, so it is also self-contradictory. It further omits that 60 of the 86 cohort shots carry no xmb group at all, so a loop's absence over the frame is partly a statement about the shot's era, not about the loop.

predict_pickup imports MachineGeometryRegistry from nova.catalog.mast_geometry (line 325, used line 331), the registry the owning plan names for retirement: nova:mast-nonaxisymmetric-physics section 5 says the saddle geometry must be read from the magnetics IDS through nova/imas/io_magnetics.py, "never through nova.catalog.mast_geometry, because machine-description-retirement deletes that registry", and to extend the owners rather than add a parallel path. The path is dead in this run (0 comparisons ran), so it is a latent break for that retirement, not a failure here, and it is outside this node's declared write paths.

gate_arms_note: the reviewed run declared no baseline_suite and no after_suite -- its evidence is a data benchmark over the level-1 store, not a pytest suite -- so added_failure_count is unmeasured (null) and added_failure_ids is empty. The review's own reproduction is the store check recorded in the run's review-evidence.log: sad_out_m010/m011/m012 present at the same 26 cohort shots as sad_out_m09 while sad_out_m10/m11/m12 are absent.
